svg.title: Dispatch pipeline and middleware phases
svg.desc: How a message passes the middleware pipeline. The in-process buses and the RabbitMQ and Kafka buses receive all BusMiddleware beans in order (by @Order or Ordered) and run only those whose phases() contain their DispatchPhase; OutboxEventBus runs none, and the outbound chain runs when the outbox relay publishes through a broker bus. LOCAL: the in-process buses SpringCommandBus, SpringQueryBus and springEventBus run the LOCAL chain and then call the handler through its registry, with no broker. OUTBOUND and INBOUND: a remote bus of the RabbitMQ or Kafka adapter (RabbitMqCommandBus, KafkaQueryBus and the others) runs the OUTBOUND chain in the sending process and then publishes; in the receiving process the consumer rehydrates the MessageContext from the context headers, runs the INBOUND chain and calls the handler through its registry. The built-in middleware, in order: ContextPropagationMiddleware (Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE; LOCAL, OUTBOUND and INBOUND); TracingMiddleware (HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 10; LOCAL and INBOUND); the opt-in RetryMiddleware (RetryMiddleware.ORDER, LOWEST_PRECEDENCE - 100; LOCAL and INBOUND); the opt-in TransactionMiddleware (TransactionMiddleware.ORDER, LOWEST_PRECEDENCE - 50; LOCAL and INBOUND), so without an outer transaction every retry attempt runs in its own transaction, while a dispatch inside an outer transaction joins it; CommandValidationInterceptor (no @Order, so LOWEST_PRECEDENCE; LOCAL, OUTBOUND and INBOUND); MicrometerBusObservability (no @Order; LOCAL and INBOUND); and your own middleware, sorted among them by its order, by default in LOCAL and INBOUND. At the end of the LOCAL and INBOUND chains the registry invokes the handler, through IdempotentInvoker when the handler is @Idempotent; at the end of the OUTBOUND chain the message is published. The animation follows a local dispatch, then a remote send and its reception, lighting the middleware each chain runs.
